assessment: This work reports that intermittent fasting alters the homeostatic regenerative programme with fundamental implications for the use of murine models to study liver regeneration and cancer and highlights through a series of solid mechanistic studies the role of FGF/Wnt signalling interactions in modulating fasted-associated regeneration. It opens up further questions as to why this occurs, how this is beneficial to adapting to a fasting state and how we should design and interpret preclinical animal studies.
